nodes.label: Guest / driver
nodes.summary: Searches, holds a unit, pays and receives a confirmation or access code.

nodes.label: Search service + index
nodes.summary: Eventually consistent view of availability by location, dates and filters. Fast, may be seconds stale, and is never trusted for the final answer.

nodes.label: Booking service
nodes.summary: Runs hold, confirm, extend and cancel. Cancels expired holds on the same range in the same transaction before inserting, and retries on serialization failures (SQLSTATE 40001) and on exclusion-constraint conflicts.
nodes.details: PostgreSQL: applications using Serializable or Repeatable Read must be prepared to retry the whole transaction.

nodes.label: Inventory DB (PostgreSQL)
nodes.summary: One row per booking with a time range. An exclusion constraint on (unit WITH =, period WITH &&) rejects overlaps. Room types use per-night counters with sold < capacity. Sharded by property or lot.
nodes.details: UNIQUE is usually unsuitable for ranges (PostgreSQL 18 adds UNIQUE ... WITHOUT OVERLAPS, enforced like an exclusion constraint). The constraint can be partial with WHERE (predicate), so cancelled bookings stop blocking. Exclusion constraints need btree_gist for scalar equality. tstzrange bounds are not canonicalised, so pass '[)' explicitly.

nodes.label: Hold sweeper
nodes.summary: Marks expired HELD bookings CANCELLED so the range is free again. Expiry is also checked at query time so a slow sweeper does not hide inventory.

nodes.label: Payment service
nodes.summary: Charges with an idempotency key derived from booking and attempt. A retry with the same key returns the saved response, and different parameters on the same key error.

nodes.label: Outbox / event stream
nodes.summary: Confirmed bookings are published reliably so email, access codes and search-index updates are not lost if the process dies after commit.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.summary: Sends confirmations, reminders and receipts. See the notification system note.

nodes.label: Gate / access control (parking)
nodes.summary: Reads a QR code or plate at entry and exit. Detects overstays, and no-shows free the space after a grace period.
nodes.details: Physical state (occupied) can differ from the booked state, so a pure calendar model is not enough.

nodes.label: Pricing service
nodes.summary: Computes price by demand, time and duration. The price is stored with the booking so later changes do not alter it.

flows.name: Book the last slot (two users race)

steps.caption: The user searches. The index says the unit is free for these dates. It may be a few seconds stale.
The user chooses it. Two users do this at the same moment.
The booking service quotes a price, to be stored with the booking.
Both transactions INSERT a HELD booking with the same unit and an overlapping period. The exclusion constraint lets one commit and rejects the other, whatever the application does.
The winner pays with an idempotency key. A network retry returns the saved result instead of charging twice.
On success the booking is marked CONFIRMED and an event is written to the outbox in the same transaction.
The outbox publishes the event, so the confirmation and access code are sent even if the process crashes after commit.
If payment never completes, the sweeper marks the hold CANCELLED after its TTL. The partial exclusion constraint stops counting it, so the range is free.
The change flows to the search index so the unit shows as available again.
The gate reports entry and exit events. A car still present after its period is an overstay, so apply the penalty policy and hold the next booking until the space is empty.
If nobody arrives within the grace period, the booking is marked NO_SHOW and the range is released for walk-ins, per policy.
